records.label: A666_21

phenotypes.text: undulating proteinuria with partial response to treatment
mesangial hypercellularity consistent with minimal change disease

quotes: The patient A666_21 was diagnosed with NS at age of 5 years. He developed SRNS at his initial presentation and was resistant to different immunosuppressive drugs.
Nevertheless, his renal function remained normal all over the time, so he stopped his clinical visits after 12.5 years of follow up.
Whole exome sequencing identifies a homozygous mutation of KIRREL1 (p.Arg440Cys) that is positioned within the maximum NPL peak on chromosome 1 (arrowhead).

records.label: B742_21
quotes: The patient B742_21 was diagnosed with NS at age of 14 years. He developed SRNS at his initial presentation.

During the course of treatment with Tacrolimus, CCB and gradual dose increase of ACE-I the patient succeeded a complete remission. However, over 4 years of follow up, he developed chronic kidney disease, which has continued to progress attaining CKD stage 2
Renal histology of individual B742_21 with KIRREL1 mutation shows focal segmental glomerular sclerosis (arrows) on light microscopy (MPAS staining).

notes.statement: Solanki et al. (2019) performed whole-exome sequencing and homozygosity mapping in 596 individuals from 406 families with SRNS and identified homozygous KIRREL1 missense mutations (R440C and S573L) in 2 individuals from unrelated consanguineous families, a frequency of 0.4%.
quotes: we performed whole-exome sequencing (WES) and homozygosity mapping in a cohort of 596 individuals from 406 families with SRNS.
We discovered two homozygous missense mutations (p.Arg440Cys and p.Ser573Leu) of the KIRREL1 gene in two individuals of unrelated consanguineous families (A666 and B742) with SRNS.

notes.statement: Solanki et al. (2019) noted that the S573L variant had an allele frequency of 0.0011 in European populations in gnomAD and was found in homozygous state in one control, raising the possibility of variable expressivity or incomplete penetrance.
quotes: Notably, the p.Ser573Leu, identified in a child of Italian descent and found mutated at the homozygous state in one control subject in GnomAD, has an allele frequency of 0.0011 in European populations, which is very frequent.
thus, there is a possibility of variable expressivity or incomplete penetrance for this variant

notes.statement: Solanki et al. (2019) found that both KIRREL1 mutants stably expressed in human podocytes mislocalized from the cell membrane and accumulated in Golgi, early endosomes, and lysosomes, without affecting NPHS1 membrane localization, and that mutant-expressing podocyte monolayers showed significantly increased albumin permeability, suggesting trafficking defects and impaired intercellular integrity.
quotes: Both KIRREL1 mutants showed increased localization at Golgi apparatus, early endosomes and lysosomes
Further, the KIRREL1 mutations did not affect membrane localization of NPHS1

In comparison to cells expressing KIRREL1 wild type protein, a significant increase in albumin flux (an indicator of increase in transepithelial permeability) was noted within 1 hour (p <0.01), with a further increase at 4 hours (p< 0.001)

notes.statement: Using immunogold electron microscopy in rodents, Liu et al. (2003) found Neph1 at the glomerular slit diaphragm. Neph1 bound directly to nephrin and ZO-1. Native and recombinant Neph1 formed dimers and multimers and bound nephrin through their extracellular segments. ZO-1 PDZ domains bound the cytoplasmic tail of Neph1.
quotes: we localize the expression of Neph1 to the glomerular slit diaphragm by immunogold electron microscopy in rodents and describe its direct interaction with two other components of the slit diaphragm, nephrin and ZO-1
Both native and recombinant Neph1 associate with each other as dimers and multimers and interact with nephrin via their extracellular segments.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2003) found that the nephrin–Neph1 interaction was specific: neither protein shared it with P-cadherin, another integral slit diaphragm protein. They concluded that the nephrin–Neph1 interaction appears to be an important determinant of glomerular permeability.
quotes: The interaction between nephrin and Neph1 is specific and not shared by either protein with P-cadherin, another integral slit diaphragm protein.
The interaction between nephrin and Neph1 therefore appears to be an important determinant of glomerular permeability.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2003) gave rodents combined subnephritogenic doses of anti-Neph1 and anti-nephrin to disrupt the Neph1–nephrin interaction. This caused proteinuria that did not depend on complement or leukocytes, and foot processes were preserved. Neph1 and nephrin protein in podocytes fell modestly and ZO-1 protein fell sharply, while mRNA levels of all three genes did not change.
quotes: Disruption of the Neph1-nephrin interaction in vivo by injecting combinations of individual subnephritogenic doses of anti-Neph1 and anti-nephrin results in complement- and leukocyte-independent proteinuria with preserved foot processes.

This disruption modestly reduces Neph1 and nephrin protein expression in podocytes and dramatically reduces ZO-1 protein expression via the interaction of ZO-1 PDZ domains with the cytoplasmic tail of Neph1, independent of changes in mRNA expression of all three genes.
